r.정치 구도: Lebanon runs on a confessional system in which religious communities share power. By convention the president is a Maronite Christian, the prime minister a Sunni Muslim and the speaker of parliament a Shia Muslim, and the 128 seats in parliament are split evenly between Christians and Muslims. The 1989 Taif Agreement, which ended a civil war that began in 1975 and lasted 15 years, reshaped this arrangement. Because posts are shared out, the state stalls whenever the parties cannot agree. The presidency sat empty for more than two years from October 2022 until a new president was elected in January 2025. In March 2026 parliament extended its own term by two years, citing the war, and postponed the May election. The biggest question in politics now is whether the state can take Hezbollah's weapons away.

t.why: Hezbollah is a Shia party backed by Iran and an armed group widely seen as stronger than the national army, which has put Lebanon on the front line between Israel and Iran. A massive Israeli air campaign in September 2024 killed Hezbollah's leader, and a ceasefire followed that November. When Hezbollah attacked Israel again in March 2026 on Iran's side, the government declared the group's military activity illegal. In June a US-brokered framework had Israeli forces pull back from some areas and the Lebanese army move in, but Israeli troops remain in a buffer zone in the south and air strikes continue. The UN peacekeeping force that has patrolled the south since 1978 ends its mandate at the close of 2026 and leaves in 2027. Lebanon also hosts one of the largest numbers of Syrian refugees in the world relative to its population.
t.rel: It has clashed often with Israel on the border and has been under a ceasefire since the 2024 war. Hezbollah holds a large military force, and the number of Syrian refugees is very high for its population.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1981, and Lebanon opened its embassy in Seoul in 1996. Since July 2007 South Korea's Dongmyeong Unit has served with the UN peacekeeping force, covering the Tyre area in the south. It is South Korea's longest-running overseas deployment of combat troops, and alongside patrol duties it has run medical care for local residents. With the UN mission winding down, the final contingent was formed in July 2026.
t.know: By convention the president is a Christian and the prime minister a Muslim, sharing power among faiths.
etext: Lebanon was long a financial hub for the Middle East. Strict banking secrecy and high interest rates drew money from the diaspora and the Gulf, and the money Lebanese abroad send home still holds the economy up.

A model that used new deposits at high interest to cover public debt broke down in 2019. The currency crashed and deposits were frozen, and the World Bank called it one of the worst economic crises anywhere since the mid-19th century. The 2020 Beirut port explosion deepened the damage. Talks with the IMF over a law deciding who absorbs the banks' losses go on, but there is still no IMF program.
Beaches, mountains, ancient ruins and food draw visitors. Many Lebanese are highly educated and speak English, French and Arabic, and large numbers work in the Gulf.

The state power company supplies only a few hours of electricity a day, so homes and shops rely on private generators. A 2022 maritime border deal with Israel opened the way to gas exploration, but the first well in 2023 found too little to develop. Each round of war cuts off tourism and investment.
